title: Trump Grants a Full Pardon to Otis Gordon on December 22, 2020
description_short: Trump granted Otis Gordon a full pardon on December 22, 2020; the official records spell his name without a middle initial.
description_medium: An archived White House statement says Trump granted Otis Gordon a full pardon on December 22, 2020. It describes his prior conviction, later ministry work and youth mentoring, and says Senator Tim Scott supported the pardon. The Justice Department’s clemency list also names Otis Gordon under the December 22 pardons and identifies the District of South Carolina.
description_long: On December 22, 2020, President Donald J. Trump granted a full pardon to Otis Gordon. The White House announcement lists Gordon among 15 people receiving full pardons that day. It says he had been convicted of possession with intent to distribute and had become a pastor at Life Changer’s International Ministries. The statement also says Gordon mentors at-risk youths in his community, led a prayer session at the U.S. Capitol after the 2015 Charleston church shooting, and was supported for clemency by Senator Tim Scott. The Justice Department’s clemency list names Otis Gordon under its December 22, 2020 pardons, identifies the District of South Carolina, and records an amended prison term of 85 or 86 months and 48 months of supervised release. It describes the offense as selling, distributing, or dispensing a controlled substance and gives January 11, 1993 as the sentence date. Both official records spell the name “Otis Gordon,” without the middle initial “W.” used in the original title.
